summary.text: Arshad Ali Khan, listed by the ABC as Arshad Khan, is standing as an independent for Dandenong at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. The ABC's guide gives no biography, and we found no campaign website or other published information about them as at 9 Nov 2026.

sources.title: Candidates for Dandenong District, Victorian Electoral Commission
Dandenong, 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Catherine D'Arcy is the Greens candidate for Dandenong at the 2026 Victorian election. She works in mental health and is an activist, and says she has spent 23 years in the area, where she brought up her three children. Her campaign centres on public housing and affordable health care.

priorities.text: to protect public housing and advocate for better affordable healthcare
More support for young people, families and multicultural communities facing homelessness and housing stress

sources.title: Dandenong: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Gabrielle Williams has been the Labor member for Dandenong since 2014 and became Deputy Premier and Labor's deputy leader in July 2026. A cabinet minister since 2018, she now holds Education, Skills and Training, First Peoples, and Women and Gender Equality, after earlier portfolios including transport, mental health and family violence prevention. She is recontesting Dandenong in 2026.

summary.text: Glenda Wright is One Nation's candidate for Dandenong at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC says she came to Australia as a child during the 1980s and has lived in the area ever since. She cites a background in senior leadership, governance, operational delivery and engagement. One Nation's candidate page could not be read for this profile.

sources.title: Dandenong: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Jack McMahon is standing for the Victorian Socialists in Dandenong at the 2026 Victorian election. Born and raised in Dandenong, he is a renter and describes himself as a community organiser and socialist activist in Melbourne's south-east. He has campaigned against racism, for migrant and First Nations communities and in support of Palestinians.

prior_roles.role: Community organiser and activist, south-eastern suburbs

priorities.text: I commit, if elected, to only take a nurse's salary
Building more public housing and properly regulating rentals
Free, universal health care, child care and schooling
Opposing over-policing in the area

sources.title: Dandenong: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Jacqueline Harvey is the Family First candidate for Dandenong at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. Her party page says she is an enrolled nurse with a nursing diploma from Australian Catholic University, has nursed in settings from aged care and GP clinics to community health and day surgery, and has spent more than 27 years in church and humanitarian work in Australia and over 25 other countries. That work included running a large volunteer team at an AIDS hospice in South Africa and a stint with the British Red Cross. A Family First candidate of the same name stood for Narre Warren South at the 2022 state election.

prior_roles.role: Volunteer coordinator, AIDS hospice in South Africa
Worked with the British Red Cross

previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia lists a Jacqueline Harvey as the Family First candidate; no source says she is the 2026 Dandenong candidate, though the name and party match.

priorities.text: Stronger families, and support for vulnerable Australians
Churches and community groups as the backbone of a caring society
Making sure every person in the community is valued and can get ahead

Dandenong, 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Jordan Forte is the Libertarian candidate for Dandenong at the 2026 Victorian election. He trained as a plumber over four years and has run online media projects; the ABC calls him a social media influencer. Since 2020 he has organised group bike rides and events around Dandenong, and the ABC notes that rides he arranged at places such as Marvel Stadium and DFO South Wharf drew media coverage.

prior_roles.role: Organiser of community group bike rides and events

priorities.text: Tackling youth crime and directing police to where they are most needed
Faster police responses to urgent calls
Protecting individual freedom and free speech

sources.title: Dandenong: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Jordan Forte, Dandenong, 2026 state election candidates, Libertarian Party Victoria

summary.text: William Billings is the Liberal candidate for Dandenong at the 2026 Victorian election. A lawyer, he heads a Melbourne criminal law practice and handles criminal and family violence matters, according to the ABC and his party. Outside the law he works as a civil marriage celebrant and performs as an artist, and his party describes him as the father of five sons.

occupation.text: Lawyer; principal of a criminal law firm

prior_roles.role: Principal
Civil marriage celebrant

priorities.text: Community safety, including 3,000 more police and protective services officers back at stations
Tougher sentencing laws
Easing cost pressures on local families and businesses
